core_obligations: The comparison map (proof lines 846-853): f = {(a, b) in A x B : the segment A_a is isomorphic to the segment B_b}, a set by Separation.
f is an isomorphism dom(f) -> ran(f) (lines 854-856): pairwise coherence from the ordinal-segment lemma.
Both pieces are initial segments (lines 857-859): downward closure of dom(f) via the initial-segment lemma; symmetrically for ran(f).

Reductio on both proper (lines 860-865): take the least a outside dom(f) and b outside ran(f); then f identifies A_a with B_b, so (a, b) should already lie in f, contradiction. Hence dom(f) = A or ran(f) = B.
proof_roadmap: Collect all segment-to-segment isomorphism pairs into f by Separation.
Show f is an isomorphism on its domain onto its range.
Show domain and range are initial segments of A and B.
Derive a contradiction if both segments are proper, using least counterexamples.
